dct_description_sm: With the increasing interest in resource exploitation and marine transport in the Arctic, there is a growing need for improved knowledge about current and future environmental conditions in the region. This initiative will build on ongoing work at Environment Canada and Fisheries and Oceans Canada to develop an operational coupled ocean-ice-atmosphere prediction system capable of predicting ocean and sea-ice conditions one month to one year in advance. The forecasts produced will support oil and gas activities by providing forecast information for planning and operations, such as infrastructure planning, transport and safety efficiency, offloading, evacuation, and ice management. Skillful predictions of sea-ice conditions one month to one season in advance will also be of benefit to northern residents. In addition, anticipated longer term changes in environmental factors relevant to human activity including sea ice and extreme wind speeds are evaluated from climate model simulations.
dct_title_s: Seasonal Forecasting of Ocean and Ice Conditions in the Beaufort Sea
